title: DistributedJacobianStrongGrowth.lean

problem_class.label: other
problem_class.details: Unconstrained operator root finding. The hidden operator F has a zero x⋆ and satisfies the one-point strong monotonicity condition ⟨F(x), x−x⋆⟩ ≥ μ‖x−x⋆‖² for every x. This makes the zero unique. The public starting point satisfies ‖x₀−x⋆‖ ≤ R.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Worker i queries a point x and receives a stochastic operator value gᵢ(x,ω) with mean F(x). The sampling maps may differ across workers. Worker i uses draw nk+i for its zero-indexed kth reply, giving fresh independent draws across workers and calls. Queries return only the sampled vector. The operator, Jacobian, root, worker maps, and sampling law are hidden.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedJacobianStrongGrowth.lean, Problem, Sampling.iid, computation.answer, oracleAssumptions, and spec. LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean, IID.

distinctive_assumptions.label: relative_error
distinctive_assumptions.details: Each worker satisfies the strong-growth bound E‖gᵢ(x,ω)‖² ≤ ρ‖F(x)‖², with public ρ ≥ 1. By unbiasedness this is equivalent to E‖gᵢ(x,ω)−F(x)‖² ≤ (ρ−1)‖F(x)‖². Every worker therefore returns zero almost surely at x⋆.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Queries, operator values, and outputs lie in Euclidean ℝᵈ with public d ≥ 1.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The mean operator is globally L-Lipschitz and Fréchet differentiable, with ‖J(x)−J(y)‖op ≤ M‖x−y‖, 0 < μ ≤ L, and M ≥ 0. These constants and the rooted tree of n ≥ 1 workers and depth at most h are public. Each worker can have one computation pending, taking τ > 0 elapsed time. Each directed tree edge can have one message pending. A b-bit payload takes l + β(b+64) time per hop, with l, β ≥ 0. Distinct workers and directed edges can operate concurrently.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedJacobianStrongGrowth.lean, Params, valid, problemAssumptions, adjacent, computation, communication, and spec.publicInput. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, Time, clockBits, OracleState, and step.

accuracy.label: distance_to_solution
accuracy.details: The point X returned from the algorithm’s root worker at the prescribed elapsed-time deadline must satisfy E‖X−x⋆‖² ≤ ε² for the public tolerance ε > 0.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedJacobianStrongGrowth.lean, valid and spec.successful. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, execute and TimedConvergence.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The output must be measurable and its squared distance to the root integrable. The expectation uses the product law of the algorithm and oracle seeds. Execution must also have finitely many events almost surely for every deadline up to the stated time budget.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedJacobianStrongGrowth.lean, spec.successful. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, law, FiniteEvents, and TimedConvergence.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup combines one-point strongly monotone root finding, a Lipschitz Jacobian of the mean operator, and worker-specific stochastic observations with relative second-moment error. Its performance criterion charges elapsed time for concurrent samples and finite-bit messages on a specified tree.

descriptionHtml:
Distributed Root Finding under Strong Growth

We seek a zero x⋆ of a Lipschitz map F:Rd→Rd in dimension d≥1. The map has a Lipschitz Jacobian and satisfies ⟨F(x),x−x⋆⟩≥μ∥x−x⋆∥2 at every point x, for some μ>0. Workers communicate over a rooted tree. At x, each worker uses a fresh independent sample to return an unbiased estimate of F(x) with second moment at most ρ∥F(x)∥2, where ρ≥1. Given a starting point within known distance of the zero and a tolerance ε>0, the goal is an output x¯ satisfying E∥x¯−x⋆∥2≤ε2 by an elapsed-time deadline, averaging over algorithm and oracle randomness.

Write E=Rd with its Euclidean inner product and norm. The equation to be solved is F(x)=0,x∈E. Let V={0,…,n−1} be the set of workers, where n≥1 is an integer. The algorithm receives d, n, the nonempty measurable sample space Ω, the tree root r, parent map p, depth function s and height bound h, the timing parameters τ,ℓ,β, the constants L,μ,ρ,M,R, the tolerance ε, and the starting point x0∈E.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Operator and Jacobian regularity). The map F is Fréchet differentiable on E. Its Jacobian J(x):E→E and the map itself satisfy, for every x,y∈E, ∥F(x)−F(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,∥J(x)−J(y)∥op≤M∥x−y∥, where 0<μ≤L, M≥0, and ∥⋅∥op is the induced operator norm.

Assumption 2 (Growth about the solution). There is a zero x⋆∈E such that, for a radius R>0, ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R,⟨F(x),x−x⋆⟩≥μ∥x−x⋆∥2(x∈E).

Assumption 3 (Sampling and strong growth). Let (ξj)j≥0 be measurable, mutually independent samples with common probability law ν on Ω, independent of the algorithm’s randomness. On its (k+1)st completed query, for k≥0, worker i∈V returns gi(x,ξnk+i) at the queried point x∈E. Each gi:E×Ω→E is jointly measurable. For each i and x, gi(x,⋅) is Bochner integrable and ∥gi(x,⋅)∥2 is integrable under ν, with Eξ∼ν[gi(x,ξ)]=F(x),Eξ∼ν[∥gi(x,ξ)∥2]≤ρ∥F(x)∥2.

Assumption 4 (Tree topology and timing). The root r∈V, parent map p:V→V, depth function s:V→{0,1,…}, and integer h≥0 satisfy p(r)=r,s(r)=0,s(i)=s(p(i))+1(i≠r),s(i)≤h(i∈V). Each worker can have one computation pending. A query accepted at time t is ready at t+τ, where τ>0. Messages travel in either direction between a nonroot worker and its parent. For a payload of b bits, the communication oracle appends 64 zero bits, so a message accepted at time t is ready at t+ℓ+β(b+64), where ℓ≥0 is the latency and β≥0 is the time per transmitted bit. The recipient receives the sender’s identity and the transmitted bit string. Each directed edge can have one message pending. Submissions to a busy worker’s computation oracle, to a busy directed edge, or to a nonneighbor are ignored. Computations on distinct workers and transmissions on distinct directed edges can overlap, including transmissions in opposite directions and communication during computation.

For an elapsed-time budget T≥0, the algorithm must almost surely process only finitely many events at every deadline t∈[0,T]. At time T, its designated output worker must produce a measurable point x¯∈E with integrable squared error satisfying E[∥x¯−x⋆∥2]≤ε2.

comparisonHtml:
The L-Lipschitz map F:Rd→Rd has an M-Lipschitz Jacobian, F(x⋆)=0, ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R, and ⟨F(x),x−x⋆⟩≥μ∥x−x⋆∥2 with 0<μ≤L. On fresh IID samples, each worker’s jointly measurable oracle satisfies Egi(x)=F(x) and E∥gi(x)∥2≤ρ∥F(x)∥2, ρ≥1. The n workers form a rooted tree of depth at most h. Each worker handles one call at a time, taking τ>0; each directed edge carries one message at a time, taking λ+βb for b bits. Distinct workers and directed edges can operate concurrently. The target is E∥x^−x⋆∥2≤ε2 under the execution law.

Elapsed-time upper bounds for distributed root finding under strong growth.

n<64κG: O(τ(1+ρκ2J)).
n≥64κG: O((τρκ2+C(n))H+τκJ+C(ndu)(κ/T)[log⁡(2u)]+).
(2) Serial extragradient (Novoselov et al. 2026, Prop. F.4) Pairwise strongly monotone. One worker, elapsed time O(τρκ(1+J)). (1): On the overlap, O(τκJ) versus O(τρκJ) when n≥64κG, J≳ρκTH and C(ndR/ε)≲Tτ. Also covers quasi-strong monotonicity. (1) needs a Lipschitz Jacobian. For n<64κG and J≥1, its bound costs a factor κ more. Startup can also dominate.
(3) Common-query minibatch extragradient (Novoselov et al. 2026, Eq. (34)) Pairwise strongly monotone. O(κmax{1,ρ/n}(1+J)) exact-vector rounds, one call per worker per round. No finite-bit time bound. (1): On a depth-h tree, local steps cut the latency term by T when hλ≍Tτ, βdlog⁡(ndR/ε)≲λ, n≥64κGT and J≳ρκTH. Gain over the cheaper of (2), (3) is then of order min{ρ,T} against uncharged bits. (1) adds Jacobian regularity and startup cost. Depth T grows at most logarithmically in n: at ρ=20, T=10 requires n≳4⋅1010κ.
(4) LESGD (Wang and Kale 2026, Thm. 1) Expected restricted gap of averaged iterates for Lipschitz monotone operators with uniformly bounded variance. (1), (4): Rates are not comparable across the distance and restricted-gap targets and noise models.
(5) LIPPAX (Wang and Kale 2026, Thm. 4) Expected restricted gap under monotonicity, Lipschitz continuity, bounded variance, a globally bounded operator and a quadratic Taylor remainder bound. (1), (5): Rates are not comparable across these operator classes and accuracy targets.

Abbr: κ=L/μ, J=log⁡(R/ε) for R>ε, G=2+ρ/8+ρ2/128, C(s)=h(λ+βdlog⁡(2+s)). In the parallel branch, T=min{⌊κ⌋,⌊log⁡(n/(64κ))/log⁡G⌋} is the local step count, q=1+32ρMRGT/μ, u=R/(εq), H=1+log⁡(dq), and [a]+=max{a,0}.

import LongTails.TemplateDistributed
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.MeasurableSpace
import Mathlib.Data.List.MinMax

open MeasureTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.DistributedJacobianStrongGrowth

open DistributedTemplate
open LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  n : ℕ+
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  root : Fin n
  parent : Fin n → Fin n
  depth : Fin n → ℕ
  h : ℕ
  τ : Time
  l : Time
  β : Time
  L : ℝ
  μ : ℝ
  ρ : ℝ
  M : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

attribute [instance] Params.measurableΩ

abbrev Point (p : Params) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d)

structure Problem (p : Params) where
  F : Point p → Point p
  J : Point p → Point p →L[ℝ] Point p
  solution : Point p

structure Sampling (p : Params) where
  Seed : Type
  [measurableSeed : MeasurableSpace Seed]
  law : ProbabilityMeasure Seed
  marginal : ProbabilityMeasure p.Ω
  sample : ℕ → Seed → p.Ω
  iid : IID sample (marginal : Measure _) (law : Measure _)

attribute [instance] Sampling.measurableSeed

structure CommReply (p : Params) where
  source : Fin p.n
  bits : List Bool

structure ComputationState (p : Params) where
  pending : Option (Time × Point p)
  samples : ℕ → p.Ω
  used : ℕ

structure CommunicationState (p : Params) where
  messages : Fin p.n → Fin p.n → Option (Time × List Bool)

def adjacent (p : Params) (source target : Fin p.n) : Prop :=
  source ≠ target ∧ (p.parent source = target ∨ p.parent target = source)

noncomputable def computation (p : Params)
    (g : Fin p.n → Point p → p.Ω → Point p) (S : Sampling p) :
    ComputationOracle (Point p) (Point p) S.Seed p.n where
  State := ComputationState p
  initial _ seed := ⟨none, fun k => S.sample k seed, 0⟩
  submit _ s time x :=
    match s.pending with
    | some _ => s
    | none => { s with pending := some (time + p.τ, x) }
  answer i s time :=
    match s.pending with
    | none => none
    | some (finish, x) =>
        if finish ≤ time then
          some (g i x (s.samples (p.n * s.used + i.val)),
            { s with pending := none, used := s.used + 1 })
        else none

noncomputable def communication (p : Params) (S : Sampling p) :
    CommunicationOracle (CommReply p) S.Seed p.n := by
  classical
  exact {
    State := CommunicationState p
    initial := fun _ => ⟨fun _ _ => none⟩
    submit := fun s time source query =>
      let (target, bits) := query
      if adjacent p source target then
        match s.messages source target with
        | some _ => s
        | none =>
            let finish := time + p.l + p.β * bits.length
            { s with messages := (Function.update s.messages source
                (Function.update (s.messages source) target (some (finish, bits)))) }
      else s
    answer := fun s time =>
      let messages := (List.finRange p.n).flatMap fun source =>
        (List.finRange p.n).filterMap fun target =>
          (s.messages source target).map fun (finish, bits) => (finish, source, target, bits)
      match List.argmin Prod.fst messages with
      | none => none
      | some (finish, source, target, bits) =>
          if finish ≤ time then
            some ((target, ⟨source, bits⟩),
              { s with messages := (Function.update s.messages source
                  (Function.update (s.messages source) target none)) })
          else none }

noncomputable def system (p : Params)
    (g : Fin p.n → Point p → p.Ω → Point p) (S : Sampling p) :
    Oracle (Point p) (Point p) (CommReply p) p.n where
  Seed := S.Seed
  law := S.law
  computation := computation p g S
  communication := communication p S

def valid (p : Params) : Prop :=
  0 < p.d ∧ p.parent p.root = p.root ∧ p.depth p.root = 0 ∧
    (∀ i, i ≠ p.root → p.depth (p.parent i) + 1 = p.depth i) ∧
    (∀ i, p.depth i ≤ p.h) ∧ 0 < p.τ ∧
    0 < p.μ ∧ p.μ ≤ p.L ∧ 1 ≤ p.ρ ∧ 0 ≤ p.M ∧ 0 < p.R ∧ 0 < p.ε ∧ Nonempty p.Ω

def problemAssumptions (p : Params) (I : Problem p) : Prop :=
  (∀ x, HasFDerivAt I.F (I.J x) x) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖I.F x - I.F y‖ ≤ p.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖I.J x - I.J y‖ ≤ p.M * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    I.F I.solution = 0 ∧ ‖p.x0 - I.solution‖ ≤ p.R ∧
    (∀ x, p.μ * ‖x - I.solution‖ ^ 2 ≤ ⟪I.F x, x - I.solution⟫)

def oracleAssumptions (p : Params) (I : Problem p)
    (g : Fin p.n → Point p → p.Ω → Point p) (S : Sampling p) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, Measurable (Function.uncurry (g i))) ∧
    (∀ i x, Integrable (g i x) (S.marginal : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ i x, Integrable (fun ω => ‖g i x ω‖ ^ 2) (S.marginal : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ i x, (∫ ω, g i x ω ∂(S.marginal : Measure _)) = I.F x) ∧
    (∀ i x, (∫ ω, ‖g i x ω‖ ^ 2 ∂(S.marginal : Measure _)) ≤ p.ρ * ‖I.F x‖ ^ 2)

noncomputable def spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  numWorkers p := p.n
  Instance := Problem
  ComputeQuery := Point
  ComputeReply := Point
  CommReply := CommReply
  Output := Point
  publicInput := id
  valid := valid
  admissible p I O := problemAssumptions p I ∧
    ∃ (g : Fin p.n → Point p → p.Ω → Point p) (S : Sampling p),
      O = system p g S ∧ oracleAssumptions p I g S
  successful p I output P := Measurable output ∧
    Integrable (fun ω => ‖output ω - I.solution‖ ^ 2) (P : Measure _) ∧
    (∫ ω, ‖output ω - I.solution‖ ^ 2 ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ p.ε ^ 2

end LongTails.Setups.DistributedJacobianStrongGrowth
